chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Abū al-Bakhtarī Wahb ibn Wahb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said:

If the sajdah is at the end of the surah, it suffices you to go into rukuʿ with it. So this does not contradict the first report, because this report is to be understood as applying to one who prays with a group and is not able to perform sajdah and then stand and recite al-Ḥamd; in that case, there is no harm in his going into rukuʿ. And the first report is to be understood as applying to one praying alone. And that which indicates this is...

key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: the prescribed prostration occurring at the end of the surah
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier hadith report being compared with this one
key_terms.الْمُنْفَرِدِ: the one praying individually, not in congregation
key_terms.تَرْكَعَ: to go into rukuʿ during salat

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile rulings about reciting a surah with sajdah at its end during salat?
ai.summary: This passage explains how two reports concerning recitation of a surah containing a sajdah at its end are to be reconciled. It states that for one praying in congregation, if performing the sajdah and then resuming recitation is not possible, going directly into rukuʿ is acceptable, while the earlier report applies to one praying alone.
